title: Preserved-Distinction Subscript Discovery
purpose: Determine whether preserved distinction needs a conditioning subscript, and if so which one.

candidate_subscript_rule.statement: A subscript on <≠> is permitted only if it specifies a tested conditioning mode that improves explanatory, predictive, or classificatory performance over the bare <≠> baseline.

root_trace_requirement.rule: Every candidate subscript x must include a proposed root-trace explanation before testing. If no root trace can be written, do not test it as formal notation.

comparison.comparison_rule: candidate_test_form must be compared directly against baseline_test_form

success_condition: A candidate subscript x is retained only if it improves at least one primary target without degrading boundary-front mediation or whole-expression pass rate.
failure_condition: If no candidate subscript beats the bare baseline, retain <≠> without subscript.
allowed_claims: PD_CG_V2R falsified the _R-conditioned improvement route within the tested model context.
<≠> remains an unpromoted candidate baseline relation.
Future subscripts must be tested against the bare preserved-distinction baseline.
blocked_claims: A new subscript is valid without comparison to baseline.
